claims.claim: President Obama signed the CARS 'cash for clunkers' program into law on June 24, 2009, as part of the Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2009.
claims.episode_span: President Obama signed the Consumer Assistance to Recycle and Save Act on 24 June 2009
claims.supporting_quote: On June 24, President Barack Obama signed the bill into law.

claims.claim: The program's name was the Consumer Assistance to Recycle and Save Program (C.A.R.S.), enacted as Title XIII of the Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2009.
claims.episode_span: Under the Car Allowance Rebate System, mechanics drained the oil
claims.supporting_quote: The Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2009 was signed into law with the Consumer Assistance to Recycle and Save Program (C.A.R.S.) as Title XIII.

claims.claim: The initial $1 billion appropriation was exhausted within days of the program opening, and Congress approved an additional $2 billion.
claims.episode_span: allocating $1 billion initially and later adding another $2 billion after the first tranche ran out in days
claims.supporting_quote: the initial $1 billion appropriated for the system was exhausted by July 30, 2009, well before the anticipated end date of November 1, 2009, due to very high demand. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] In response, Congress approved an additional $2 billion.

claims.claim: Claims processing began July 24, 2009, the program ended August 24, 2009 when funds were exhausted, and 677,081 vehicles were scrapped.
claims.episode_span: opened the program on 24 July and closed it on 24 August once funds were exhausted
claims.supporting_quote: the processing of claims began July 24, [ 2 ] and the program ended on August 24, 2009, as the appropriated funds were exhausted, having scrapped 677,081 vehicles.

claims.claim: Rebate vouchers were fixed at either $3,500 or $4,500 per eligible trade-in.
claims.episode_span: offered fixed rebates of $3,500 or $4,500 to consumers who traded in vehicles meeting age and mileage thresholds
claims.supporting_quote: the amount of the credit given in the form of vouchers to eligible customers was either $3,500 or $4,500

claims.claim: Qualifying new passenger cars had to achieve a combined fuel economy of at least 22 mpg.
claims.episode_span: for newer models that achieved at least 22 miles per gallon combined
claims.supporting_quote: for passenger automobiles, the new vehicle must have a combined fuel economy value of at least 22 mpg

claims.claim: Trade-in engines were permanently destroyed by draining the oil, replacing it with sodium silicate, and running the engine until it seized.
claims.episode_span: mechanics drained the oil, ran the engines until they seized, and then crushed the vehicles
claims.supporting_quote: The motor oil is drained and replaced with a sodium silicate solution. The engine is started and run until the solution becomes glass-like when heated, causing the engine's internal bearings, pistons and piston rings to abrade and ultimately seize.

claims.claim: Economists Mian and Sufi found about 360,000 purchases were induced in July-August 2009 but most were merely brought forward, giving the program a muted total effect on auto purchases.
claims.episode_span: The program also pulled forward purchases that would have occurred anyway, so the net addition to the total fleet was smaller
claims.source_title: Cash for Clunkers Had Modest and Short-Lived Effects | NBER
claims.supporting_quote: About 360,000 automobile purchases were induced in July and August 2009. Most of these purchases simply were brought forward by a few months: a sharp decline in sales after the program ended suggests that it had a muted total effect on auto purchases
